reply_text:
Opening The Batch essay and a Lex Fridman transcript.I found four dated predictions from 2020. Three come from Sutskever's own short essay in The Batch, published 30 December 2020. The fourth comes from his May 2020 appearance on the Lex Fridman Podcast. It is weak, and the only text I could read is a machine transcript.

**The Batch essay (his own words; publication date read from the page's metadata)**
- He expected "the best models of 2021 will make the best models of 2020 look dull and simple-minded by comparison."
- He wrote "In 2021, language models will start to become aware of the visual world," and that the next generation would edit and generate images from text.
- He said models that see text and images together might learn concepts more as humans do, calling this "an aspiration" he hoped to see "in 2021." This one is a hope rather than a firm forecast.

**Lex Fridman Podcast #94**
- He agreed that true human-level language understanding and visual perception could not be fully solved "in the next three months." He then said his guess beyond that was as good as anyone's.
- **Where the words come from:** the wording comes from podscripts.co, an unofficial machine transcript. A second machine transcript (swellai) has a garbled version of the same passage, and I did not check against the recording.
- **Episode date:** May 2020. The Apple Podcasts listing in a search result gives 8 May 2020, but I didn't open that page, so check the exact day.

**Gaps**
- **Where his timing remarks would be:** all three transcript pages I opened stop at about the 32-minute mark. The "How to build AGI?" (1:13:41) and "Question to AGI" (1:25:00) segments are later, so I could not read them. I found no undated AGI-timing quote for 2020.
- **Page that failed:** one page I opened (transcript.lol) loaded only the site's homepage.
- **Searches:** the three fixed searches returned only 2025 news about his "age of scaling" and "5 to 20 years" remarks.
